global_structure: Ancient stone amphitheater viewed straight on. Six horizontal stone seating tiers rise from foreground to background. A seventh rear wall spans behind the upper tier. A tall rigid rectangular stone frame stands at the exact top-center position. The frame has straight vertical sides, a straight top edge, sharp corners and a clear rectangular opening. The amphitheater geometry, tier boundaries, frame proportions, frontal perspective and overall composition remain fixed and unchanged. Center tiers (tiers 3-4) are empty for performers. Vertical wall elements are minimized through masking techniques, with side compositions emphasized.
global_frame_rule: The central rectangular stone frame is a permanent architectural invariant. Do not move, distort, widen, narrow, tilt, decorate, replace or break it. Preserve its exact rectangular silhouette and vertical symmetry. Any moon or celestial disk must appear only inside the rectangular opening of the frame, never above, behind, beside or outside it. Center area within the frame opening is empty for performance use.
